response.consequence: The anonymous device limit can be bypassed. A device that was rejected is let in on its second request and stays in for up to 29 minutes, without ever being recorded in anon_device. Enforcement is therefore inconsistent: the first request is denied and later ones are allowed.
response.explanation: Authenticate now returns an error when TagDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached (client.go:44-47). In impl.go, tagDeviceUI calls localCache.SetDefault(key) at line 87, before CreateOrUpdateDevice at line 93. When that call fails with ErrDeviceLimitReached, the cache entry stays. The next request with the same device ID and the same cache key within the 29-minute TTL hits `localCache.Get` and returns nil at line 83. TagDevice then returns nil and Authenticate grants anonymous access, even though the device was never stored and the limit is still reached.

other_findings.consequence: The number of stored devices can exceed device_limit under concurrent first-time requests.
other_findings.explanation: CreateOrUpdateDevice runs CountDevices and then a separate INSERT (lines 107-118 and below) with no transaction or lock. Concurrent new devices can all read count < limit and all insert.
